source.basis: The common kinds of tax-exempt organization and how the Internal Revenue Code treats each, as recalled from IRS Publications 557 (Tax-Exempt Status for Your Organization), 526 (Charitable Contributions) and 15 (Employer's Tax Guide), and the FUTA and state unemployment exclusions (IRC sections 3306(c)(8) and 3309(b)(1)); a private foundation's payout, excise and donor limit from IRC sections 4940, 4942 and 170(b)(1)(B) and the Instructions for Form 990-PF; who may hold an S corporation's shares from IRC section 1361(c)(6); not queried live. Treat as plausible defaults, not legal advice.

code.doc: The Internal Revenue Code section that exempts it.

income_tax_exempt.doc: Pays no income tax on its income.

donations_deductible.doc: A person's cash gifts to it are deductible.

futa.doc: Owes federal unemployment tax on its staff's wages.

suta.doc: Owes state unemployment tax on its staff's wages.

s_corp_holder.doc: May hold an S corporation's shares (IRC section 1361(c)(6)).

payout_pct.doc: A private foundation's minimum payout a year, of the average value of its assets (IRC section 4942(e)).

excise_pct.doc: A private foundation's excise on its net investment income (IRC section 4940(a)).

undistributed_tax_pct.doc: A private foundation's tax on a payout still ungranted a year late (IRC section 4942(a)).

donor_limit_pct.doc: The share of a person's income their deductible gifts to it may come to (IRC section 170(b)(1)(B)).

charity.name: Charity or nonprofit
charity.description: A public charity or other nonprofit organized for charitable, educational, scientific or literary purposes: a food bank, a shelter, a school, a museum. Gifts to it are deductible; it owes no FUTA but pays state unemployment tax.

church.name: Church or religious organization
church.description: A church, synagogue, mosque, temple or other religious organization, exempt without applying. Gifts to it are deductible; it owes neither FUTA nor state unemployment tax.

club.name: Social club
club.description: A club organized for pleasure and recreation, supported by its members' dues: a country club, a hobby or sports club, a fraternal lodge's social arm. Exempt on its members' money, but gifts to it are not deductible, and it pays unemployment taxes like any employer.

private_foundation.name: Private foundation
private_foundation.description: A charity funded by one family, company or founder rather than the public: a family foundation, a company's foundation. It grants out at least 5% of the average value of its assets each year, by the end of the next, last year's shortfall first; it pays 1.39% on its net investment income and 30% on a payout still ungranted a year late, both with its return on 15 May. A person deducts gifts to it up to 30% of their income.
